indicator_definition: The housing cost overburden rate is the proportion of the population living in households where total housing costs (net of housing allowances) represent more than 40% of total disposable household income. It is expressed as a percentage. Data are based on the EU Statistics on Income and Living Conditions (EU-SILC).
rationale: Excessive housing costs reduce disposable income available for other necessities and increase the risk of poverty and social exclusion. Monitoring this indicator helps identify households under financial strain from housing costs. Progress means a reduction in the proportion of people overburdened by housing costs.
methodology_characteristics: Data are collected through EU-SILC. Housing costs include rent, mortgage repayments, utilities and maintenance. Housing allowances are deducted from both costs and income before calculating the 40% threshold. The survey is conducted annually.
